description: [needs a free API key — this call will fail without one: https://visa.orizn.app/visa-api/register?source=mcp-remote, then reconnect with ?key=<key>] THE default visa tool: the full entry record for ONE passport travelling to ONE destination. Returns the requirement (visa_free / visa_required / e_visa / visa_on_arrival / eta / no_admission), days allowed, a written description, required documents, application steps, visa types, cost, validity, max stay, processing time, passport validity months, visa fees, photo specs, vaccinations, insurance, safety advisory, health requirements, overstay penalties, entry by mode (air/land/sea), transit rules, remote-work visa, extension rules, minor rules, dual-nationality and passport-stamp warnings, and embassies — in any of 15 languages, on every plan including free (fr, en, es, pt, de, ja, ko, zh, ru, it, ar, hi, th, vi, tl). Call it whenever the user asks whether they need a visa, what documents or vaccinations are needed, what a visa costs, how long it takes, how long they can stay, or what happens if they overstay. Needs an Orizn API key on this MCP connection and costs 1 request against that key's monthly quota. On the free plan the deep fields come back as {upgrade: "Available on Starter plan or above"} instead of data — report that as a plan limit, never as missing data. Reading the reply: every deep field carries a `granularity`. "destination" means the value describes the destination country for all nationalities (fees, processing days, transit, overstay, safety); "passport" means it describes the passport for all destinations (reciprocity history, stamp and dual-nationality warnings). Only the requirement, visa-free days, description and documents are pair-specific. A field Orizn does not have comes back as {status: "unavailable"} — say so rather than filling the gap, and `as_of` is the reference date of that field, not live data.

destination.description: Country being entered, ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 (e.g. JPN for Japan).

lang.description: Language of the written fields. One of: fr, en, es, pt, de, ja, ko, zh, ru, it, ar, hi, th, vi, tl. Defaults to en. Available on every plan, free included.

passport.description: Passport country, ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 (e.g. FRA for France).
